strategy: Run the broad cartservice recovery test first, then—after the shop has recovered—test the narrower checkout-only payment failure. The two-experiment budget cannot cover three distinct failure classes; these experiments cover recovery and errors while using different experiment types and services.

spec.reason: Ranked first because cartservice is a single replica, has high risk, is shared by frontend and checkoutservice, and reaches all five flows. Prior cartservice pod kills affected all flows with peak errors near 90–100% and recovery around 22–31 seconds, making this the broadest shopper-visible test.
spec.hypothesis: The killed cartservice pod will cause visible errors across shopping and checkout flows until Kubernetes replaces it; recovery will take tens of seconds. The brief outage is expected to complete rather than be stopped by the guard, consistent with prior cartservice pod-kill runs.

experiments.learning_goal: Measure the shopper-visible blast radius and recovery time when the single cartservice pod is killed.

spec.reason: Ranked second because paymentservice is a single replica on the revenue-critical checkout path, but its reach is limited to checkout. Prior 30-second paymentservice failures affected checkout; observed peak error rates around 21% show this failure is visible and may activate the guard.
spec.hypothesis: With paymentservice unavailable, checkout attempts will fail while the other flows remain usable. Errors should dominate rather than latency; the guard is likely to abort if the checkout error threshold is exceeded on consecutive checks.

experiments.learning_goal: Verify whether checkout errors from a sustained payment dependency outage cross the safety guard threshold, and confirm isolation from other shopper flows.

skipped_ideas.why_not: Prior +100 ms already made pages roughly 700 ms slower across all flows, and the service is called sequentially multiple times; this stronger slowdown risks tripping the p95 guard rather than providing a controlled shopper-visible slowdown test.
A prior 200-user run reached p95 1578 ms and was guard-aborted. The frontend is also the single-replica entrypoint, so this recipe risks broadly disrupting shoppers.
A prior run at this intensity was guard-aborted with high errors across all flows and a cartservice restart; the selected cartservice test already provides the broad cart-path failure measurement.
